I read the whole file: compact_gibbs_ibp, adjointCoordinate_compact_pairing, tensorAdjoint_compact_pairing, standardGaussian_eq_gibbs and compact_gaussian_ibp. I also grepped the repository for the continuity idiom `(h.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)).clm_apply continuous_const`. It appears about 8 times in this file and in many others. In this file it is a one-line term, used to prove `Continuous (directional v f)`. A one-line term is not nontrivial repeated reasoning. PolyC1.lean already has `directional_continuous`, but it is stated for `PolyC1`, not for `ContDiff ℝ 1`, so it is not a direct replacement.

The other repeated pieces are also small:
- The two-line `probability_gibbs_of_partition` instance setup appears in two lemmas.
- The `h2` integrability term in adjointCoordinate_compact_pairing and in tensorAdjoint_compact_pairing is the same compact-support integrability argument. It differs in its hypotheses and arguments, and it takes only a few lines.

Abstracting any of these would be a thin wrapper or a short routine step. Under the rubric that does not justify a shared lemma. The Gaussian lemmas in the second half do not repeat reasoning from the first half; they only apply it. I found no justified finding.
